metaTitle: Mercedes-Benz Engine Inspection & Assessment | Mercedes Garage
metaDescription: Professional engine inspection and assessment for all Mercedes-Benz models. Full teardown, precision measurement, crack testing, and reusability evaluation with a detailed repair plan.
lede: Comprehensive engine inspection and assessment for all Mercedes-Benz models. Full teardown, precision measurement, crack testing, and a detailed repair plan.

blocks.html: Our engine inspection and assessment service provides a complete, transparent evaluation of your Mercedes-Benz engine. We follow a structured process to determine the condition of every component and recommend the most appropriate course of action.

items: **Initial visual check** – external inspection for leaks, overheating signs, and visible damage
**Complete disassembly** – strip the engine down to its core components: block, crankshaft, connecting rods, cylinder head, and valvetrain
**Critical measurements** – block deck flatness, cylinder bore wear, crankshaft journal condition, connecting rod straightness and big-end bore
**Crack testing** – dye-penetrant (visible/fluorescent) and magnetic-particle inspection on machined parts to detect surface and sub-surface cracks
**Reusability determination** – assess each component against manufacturer specifications; decide which parts can be reused, which require machining, and which must be replaced
**Quotation and repair plan** – provide a detailed, fixed-price quotation for the required rebuild or replacement, with a clear roadmap of work

blocks.html: All measurements are performed with certified precision instruments, and our findings are documented for your reference. We also offer a second-opinion assessment for engines that have been previously diagnosed elsewhere.

Our inspection and assessment fee is deducted from the final rebuild or replacement cost. The table below shows our rebuild starting prices – your quotation will be based on the actual condition of your engine.

paras: [Pricing disclaimer](/pricing-legal-disclaimer) – the inspection fee is waived if you proceed with the rebuild. Contact us for a detailed quote after assessment.

steps.title: Arrival & Visual Check
steps.body: Vehicle arrives at our workshop. We perform a thorough external inspection, document any leaks, overheating signs, or visible damage.

steps.title: Complete Disassembly
steps.body: Engine is stripped down to its bare components – block, crank, rods, cylinder head, valvetrain, and all ancillary parts.

steps.title: Precision Measurement
steps.body: All critical dimensions are measured: deck flatness, bore wear, journal taper and ovality, rod straightness and big-end size.

steps.title: Crack Testing & Reusability
steps.body: Dye-penetrant or magnetic-particle inspection on key components. Each part is assessed against Mercedes factory specifications.

steps.title: Quotation & Repair Plan
steps.body: We compile all findings into a detailed report. You receive a fixed-price quotation for the required rebuild or replacement.

steps.title: Decision & Next Steps
steps.body: You approve the plan, and we move forward – either with a rebuild (including in-house machining) or, if needed, a replacement.

items.q: What does a Mercedes-Benz engine inspection and assessment involve?
items.a: It includes a full visual check, complete disassembly, precision measurement of block deck flatness, bore wear, crankshaft journals, and connecting rods, dye-penetrant or magnetic-particle crack testing, and a reusability determination for all components. The outcome is a detailed repair plan and fixed-price quotation.

items.q: How long does an inspection take before I get a quote?
items.a: The disassembly, cleaning, and inspection phase typically takes 1–3 days. We aim to provide your quotation within this timeframe, though machining or external specialist assessments may add a few days.

items.q: What equipment do you use for crack testing?
items.a: We use dye-penetrant (visible or fluorescent) and magnetic-particle inspection methods, depending on the material and component. This identifies surface and sub-surface cracks that might compromise the engine's integrity.

items.q: Do you machine the block and crank in-house or outsource it?
items.a: We perform all our own machining in-house at our Billericay workshop. This includes cylinder boring and honing, deck resurfacing, align honing, and crankshaft grinding. We do not outsource any critical operations.

items.q: How long does the whole rebuild process take after assessment?
items.a: The total journey from assessment to completion can range from a few days to a couple of weeks, depending on parts availability and the scope of machining required. Most rebuilds are completed within 3–5 working days once the parts are sourced.
